title: A London Day Out With Teens: Ideas That Aren’t Boring
description: Plan a London day out with teenagers: free museums with a twist, markets, river trips, Platform 9¾, the Studio Tour and viewpoints, plus how to keep costs down.
h1: A London day out with teenagers
intro: London has plenty to impress even the hardest-to-please teenager, and lots of it is free. Here’s a day that mixes iconic sights with things they’ll actually post.

cardText: Free museums, markets, river views and Harry Potter stops.

blocks.title: Scout’s London route
blocks.text: Let your teen plan one stop. Then mix one free museum, one food market and one view, and finish on the South Bank.
points: Travel by train and check 2FOR1 offers
Contactless works on the Tube but not for 2FOR1

sections.html:
• The Science Museum and Natural History Museum are free.
  • The South Bank riverside walk: street performers, skateboarders at the undercroft and views of Parliament.
  • Platform 9¾ at King’s Cross for a photo.

• The Harry Potter Studio Tour: book well ahead.
  • The Tower of London: Crown Jewels and Yeoman Warder tours.
  • A West End show (look for matinee and day-seat offers at the theatre).
Use National Rail 2FOR1 offers with paper or e-tickets, picnic in a royal park, and pick one paid attraction, not three. Visiting from abroad? Check the UK ETA.

faqs.q: What is there to do in London for teenagers?
faqs.a: Free museums, the South Bank, markets, Platform 9¾, the Tower of London, the Harry Potter Studio Tour and West End shows are all popular with teens.
